q: A _____ is a shorthand notation of an element.
e: A symbol is a shorthand notation of an element. Symbol is the idea that completes this fact. Formula would fill a different blank than symbol.

q: When the names of two or more elements begin with the same letter, the first letter together with _____ in the name of an element is chosen as the symbol.
e: When the names of two or more elements begin with the same letter, the first letter together with another letter in the name of an element is chosen as the symbol. Another letter is the idea that completes this fact. A number would fill a different blank than another letter.

q: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Natrium' is _____.
e: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Natrium' is Na. Na is the idea that completes this fact. K would fill a different blank than Na.

q: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Ferrum' is _____.
e: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Ferrum' is Fe. Fe is the idea that completes this fact. Ag would fill a different blank than Fe.

q: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Plumbum' is _____.
e: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Plumbum' is Pb. Pb is the idea that completes this fact. Sn would fill a different blank than Pb.

q: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Cuprum' is _____.
e: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Cuprum' is Cu. Cu is the idea that completes this fact. Cr would fill a different blank than Cu.

q: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Argentum' is _____.
e: The symbol for the element with the Latin name 'Argentum' is Ag. Ag is the idea that completes this fact. Al would fill a different blank than Ag.

q: A molecular formula is a shorthand notation representing a molecule or a compound of a substance, and it shows the _____ contained in a molecule or a compound.
e: A molecular formula is a shorthand notation representing a molecule or a compound of a substance, and it shows the number of atoms contained in a molecule or a compound. Number of atoms is the idea that completes this fact. Types of bonds would fill a different blank than number of atoms.

q: For compounds which exist in the form of giant structure, a formula represents the _____ of the compound.
e: For compounds which exist in the form of giant structure, a formula represents the simplest unit of the compound. Simplest unit is the idea that completes this fact. Molecular mass would fill a different blank than simplest unit.

q: As compounds of giant structure do not have separate molecules, they cannot have molecular mass, so _____ is used instead.
e: As compounds of giant structure do not have separate molecules, they cannot have molecular mass, so formula mass is used instead. Formula mass is the idea that completes this fact. Molar mass is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: The empirical formula of a compound is the _____ formula of the compound.
e: The empirical formula of a compound is the simplest formula of the compound. An empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound. Actual would fill a different blank than simplest.

q: The empirical formula shows the types of elements present in the compound and the _____ of the different types of the atoms in the compound.
e: The empirical formula shows the types of elements present in the compound and the simplest ratio of the different types of the atoms in the compound. Simplest ratio is the idea that completes this fact. Molecular ratio would fill a different blank than simplest ratio.

q: When the empirical and molecular formulae of a compound are different, the molecular formula is always a _____ of the empirical formula.
e: When the empirical and molecular formulae of a compound are different, the molecular formula is always a multiple of the empirical formula. Multiple is the idea that completes this fact. Fraction would fill a different blank than multiple.

q: The combining capacity or valence of an element is represented by the number of atoms of hydrogen, chlorine, or _____ that combine with one atom of that element.
e: The combining capacity or valence of an element is represented by the number of atoms of hydrogen, chlorine, or sodium that combine with one atom of that element. Sodium is the idea that completes this fact. Nitrogen would fill a different blank than sodium.

q: _____ describes the combining capacity of the element and also indicates the positive and negative nature of its atoms in the compounds.
e: Oxidation number describes the combining capacity of the element and also indicates the positive and negative nature of its atoms in the compounds. Oxidation number is a bookkeeping charge that tracks electron transfer. Atomic mass would fill a different blank than Oxidation number.

q: In compounds formed by the combination of metals with non-metals, the metals always show _____ character.
e: In compounds formed by the combination of metals with non-metals, the metals always show electropositive character. Electropositive is the idea that completes this fact. Electronegative would fill a different blank than electropositive.

q: In the formula of a binary compound, the algebraic sum of the _____ must be equal to zero.
e: In the formula of a binary compound, the algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers must be equal to zero. Oxidation number is a bookkeeping charge that tracks electron transfer. Molecular masses would fill a different blank than oxidation numbers.

q: Binary compounds in which the more electropositive element has a fixed oxidation number are named with the second element ending in the syllable _____.
e: Binary compounds in which the more electropositive element has a fixed oxidation number are named with the second element ending in the syllable -ide. -ide is the idea that completes this fact. -ite would fill a different blank than -ide.

q: For the naming of non-metallic binary compounds with variable oxidation numbers, _____ are used to indicate the number of atoms of each element.
e: For the naming of non-metallic binary compounds with variable oxidation numbers, Greek prefixes are used to indicate the number of atoms of each element. Greek prefixes is the idea that completes this fact. Roman numerals would fill a different blank than Greek prefixes.

q: For naming metallic binary compounds with variable oxidation numbers, the name of the metal is followed by a _____ in brackets to state its oxidation number.
e: For naming metallic binary compounds with variable oxidation numbers, the name of the metal is followed by a Roman Numeral in brackets to state its oxidation number. Roman Numeral is the idea that completes this fact. Greek prefix would fill a different blank than Roman Numeral.

q: In naming acids which have hydrogen atoms in their molecules, the name of the acid radical '-ic' is changed to _____.
e: In naming acids which have hydrogen atoms in their molecules, the name of the acid radical '-ic' is changed to -ide. -ide is the idea that completes this fact. -ous would fill a different blank than -ide.

q: In naming acids which have oxygen atoms in their molecules, the acid radical '-ous acid' is changed to _____.
e: In naming acids which have oxygen atoms in their molecules, the acid radical '-ous acid' is changed to -ite. -ite is the idea that completes this fact. -ate would fill a different blank than -ite.

q: The ion formed after removal of hydroxide ions ($OH^-$) from a base is called a _____.
e: The ion formed after removal of hydroxide ions (OH-) from a base is called a basic radical. Basic radical is the idea that completes this fact. Spectator ion would fill a different blank than basic radical.

q: The formula of a salt consists of two parts: the first part is the metal atom or the ammonium radical, and the second part is the _____.
e: The formula of a salt consists of two parts: the first part is the metal atom or the ammonium radical, and the second part is the acid radical. Acid radical is the idea that completes this fact. Hydroxide radical would fill a different blank than acid radical.

q: The empirical formula shows the simplest _____ ratio of atoms in a compound.
e: The empirical formula shows the simplest whole number ratio of atoms in a compound. An empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound. Decimal would fill a different blank than whole number.

q: The molecular formula shows the _____ number of atoms of each element present in one molecule or one formula unit of the compound.
e: The molecular formula shows the total number of atoms of each element present in one molecule or one formula unit of the compound. Total is the idea that completes this fact. Ratio would fill a different blank than total.

q: The oxidation number is related to, but not identical with, _____ or combining capacity.
e: The oxidation number is related to, but not identical with, valence or combining capacity. Valence tells how many electrons an atom typically uses in bonding. Atomic number is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: In a binary compound, the more electropositive element present in the compound with a positive oxidation number is written in _____ of the symbol of the element with a negative oxidation number.
e: In a binary compound, the more electropositive element present in the compound with a positive oxidation number is written in front of the symbol of the element with a negative oxidation number. Front is the idea that completes this fact. Middle would fill a different blank than front.

q: One exception to the order of symbols in a binary compound is $NH_3$, in which the symbol with a negative oxidation number (N) is written _____.
e: One exception to the order of symbols in a binary compound is NH3, in which the symbol with a negative oxidation number (N) is written first. First is the idea that completes this fact. Last would fill a different blank than first.

q: The acid radical $SO_4^{2-}$ is named as _____.
e: The acid radical SO42- is named as sulphate. Sulphate is the idea that completes this fact. Hydrogen sulphate would fill a different blank than sulphate.

q: The name of the acid radical $NO_2^-$ derived from nitrous acid ($HNO_2$) is _____.
e: The name of the acid radical NO2- derived from nitrous acid (HNO2) is nitrite. Nitrite is the idea that completes this fact. Nitride would fill a different blank than nitrite.

q: The basic radical formed when $NaOH$ loses an $OH^-$ ion is _____.
e: The basic radical formed when NaOH loses an OH- ion is Na+. Na+ is the idea that completes this fact. OH+ would fill a different blank than Na+.

q: All hydroxides include one or more $-OH$ radicals of oxidation number _____ in their formulae.
e: All hydroxides include one or more -OH radicals of oxidation number -1 in their formulae. -1 is the idea that completes this fact. +1 would fill a different blank than -1.

q: Hydroxides are named in the same way as the naming of salts, but the name of the acid radical is replaced by the word _____.
e: Hydroxides are named in the same way as the naming of salts, but the name of the acid radical is replaced by the word hydroxide. Hydroxide is the idea that completes this fact. Hydrate would fill a different blank than hydroxide.

q: The empirical formula of phosphorus(V) oxide is _____, while its actual molecular formula is $P_4O_{10}$.
e: The empirical formula of phosphorus(V) oxide is P2O5, while its actual molecular formula is P4O10. P2O5 is the idea that completes this fact. PO5 would fill a different blank than P2O5.

q: The molecular formula is always a multiple of the empirical formula, expressed as molecular formula = _____ $\times$ empirical formula.
e: The molecular formula is always a multiple of the empirical formula, expressed as molecular formula = n x empirical formula. N is the idea that completes this fact. X would fill a different blank than n.

q: In the compound $NaCl$, the oxidation number of sodium is _____.
e: In the compound NaCl, the oxidation number of sodium is +1. +1 is the idea that completes this fact. -1 would fill a different blank than +1.

q: In the compound $HCl$, the more electropositive element hydrogen is assigned an oxidation number of _____.
e: In the compound HCl, the more electropositive element hydrogen is assigned an oxidation number of +1. +1 is the idea that completes this fact. -1 would fill a different blank than +1.

q: In naming salts, the name begins with the name of the metal or ammonium radical, followed by the name of the _____.
e: In naming salts, the name begins with the name of the metal or ammonium radical, followed by the name of the acid radical. Acid radical is the idea that completes this fact. Basic radical would fill a different blank than acid radical.

q: The formula of sodium sulphate is _____ because the sum of the oxidation numbers must be equal to zero.
e: The formula of sodium sulphate is Na2SO4 because the sum of the oxidation numbers must be equal to zero. Na2SO4 is the idea that completes this fact. Na(SO4)2 would fill a different blank than Na2SO4.

q: The name of the compound $FeCl_2$ is _____ because iron has a variable oxidation number.
e: The name of the compound FeCl2 is iron(II) chloride because iron has a variable oxidation number. Iron(II) chloride is the idea that completes this fact. Iron(III) chloride would fill a different blank than iron(II) chloride.

q: The name of the compound $Cu_2O$ is _____.
e: The name of the compound Cu2O is copper(I) oxide. Copper(I) oxide is the idea that completes this fact. Copper(II) oxide would fill a different blank than copper(I) oxide.

q: The name of the compound $N_2O$ using Greek prefixes is _____.
e: The name of the compound N2O using Greek prefixes is dinitrogen monoxide. Dinitrogen monoxide is the idea that completes this fact. Dinitrogen oxide would fill a different blank than dinitrogen monoxide.

q: The name of the compound $CCl_4$ using Greek prefixes is _____.
e: The name of the compound CCl4 using Greek prefixes is carbon tetrachloride. Carbon tetrachloride is the idea that completes this fact. Tetracarbon chloride would fill a different blank than carbon tetrachloride.

q: The formula for ammonium sulphate is _____.
e: The formula for ammonium sulphate is (NH4)2SO4. (NH4)2SO4 is the idea that completes this fact. NH4SO4 would fill a different blank than (NH4)2SO4.

q: The formula for calcium hydrogen carbonate is _____.
e: The formula for calcium hydrogen carbonate is Ca(HCO3)2. Ca(HCO3)2 is the idea that completes this fact. CaHCO3 would fill a different blank than Ca(HCO3)2.

q: The formula for iron(III) hydroxide is _____.
e: The formula for iron(III) hydroxide is Fe(OH)3. Fe(OH)3 is the idea that completes this fact. Fe(OH)2 would fill a different blank than Fe(OH)3.

q: The acid radical $HSO_4^-$ is named as _____.
e: The acid radical HSO4- is named as hydrogen sulphate. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab. Sulphate would fill a different blank than hydrogen sulphate.
